chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Muskhan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about this verse: 'There is no blame upon you for what you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers,' until the end of the verse. I said, 'What does He mean by His saying, 'or your friends'?' He said, 'By Allah, it is that a man enters the house of his friend and eats without his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'or your friends' mean in the context of eating in their houses?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the phrase 'or your friends' in Surah al-Nur (24:61) permits entering a close friend's home and eating without seeking explicit permission, highlighting the legal concept of *ma'ruf* (customary familiarity) in social interactions. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the rights of close companions (*suhba*) and the relaxation of formalities among those with established trust and intimacy.
